Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.Gene Regulation and Expression: Experiments probing how genes are turned on/off; transcription factors; epigenetic regulation (e.g. chromatin modifications, DNA methylation); promoter/enhancer studies; non‐coding RNA roles.
Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.Protein Biochemistry and Enzymology: Study of protein structure, folding, dynamics, catalytic mechanisms of enzymes; post‐translational modifications; protein interactions; kinetics; inhibitor/drug binding assays.
Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.Structural Biology: Determination of molecular structures by X-ray crystallography, cryo‐EM, NMR, small‐angle scattering; structure‐function experiments; mutagenesis to test structure predictions.
Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.Cell and Organelle Biology: Cellular architecture; membrane trafficking; organelle biogenesis and dynamics; cytoskeleton; live cell imaging; intracellular signaling; cell adhesion.
Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.Metabolism and Metabolic Regulation: Metabolic pathway elucidation; flux analysis; metabolomics; regulation of metabolic enzymes; metabolic adaptation to environment; energy homeostasis.

Genetics Genomics and Epigenetics.Classical Genetics: Inheritance, mutant phenotypes, linkage mapping, crossing experiments, gene knockouts or overexpression in organisms.
Genetics Genomics and Epigenetics.Population Genetics: Empirical measurement of allele frequencies across populations; field sampling; studies of genetic drift, gene flow, selection in natural or experimental populations.
Genetics Genomics and Epigenetics.Genomics and Comparative Genomics: Sequencing of genomes; comparative genome analysis; identification of genomic variation; structural variation; large-scale genome projects.
Genetics Genomics and Epigenetics.Epigenetics and Phenotypic Plasticity: How environmental or developmental cues shape epigenetic marks; experiments on epigenetic inheritance; effects of diet, stress, etc.; chromatin accessibility assays.
Genetics Genomics and Epigenetics.Functional Genomics: High‐throughput screening (RNAi, CRISPR) to test gene function; transcriptomics (RNA-seq), proteomics to associate genes with phenotypes; single‐cell genomics.

Cell Development Organismal Biology.Developmental Biology: Studies of embryogenesis; cell differentiation; morphogenesis; organ formation; patterning; stem cell biology; regeneration.
Cell Development Organismal Biology.Cell Cycle Death and Apoptosis: Regulation of cell division; checkpoints; programmed cell death; senescence; proliferation control and its dysregulation (e.g. cancer).
Cell Development Organismal Biology.Physiology at Cell and Organ Level: Function of organs and tissues; signaling; transport; homeostasis; organ systems' response to stimuli; stress, temperature, etc.
Cell Development Organismal Biology.Regenerative Biology and Stem Cells: Tissue repair; stem cell niches; induced pluripotent stem cells; organoid models; regeneration in organisms.
Cell Development Organismal Biology.Aging and Longevity: Experimental studies of aging mechanisms; genetics of lifespan; cellular senescence; caloric restriction; model organisms for aging.

Microbiology Infectious Disease and Immu.Microbial Physiology and Cell Biology: Growth, metabolism, and structural biology of bacteria, archaea, fungi, protists; cell wall biology; biofilm formation.
Microbiology Infectious Disease and Immu.Pathogenesis andHost Pathogen Interactio: Molecular, cellular experiments of how pathogens infect hosts; immune evasion; virulence factors; experimental infection models.
Microbiology Infectious Disease and Immu.Virology: Virus replication; viral entry; antiviral drug testing; vaccine development; virus‐host interactions; viral evolution experiments.
Microbiology Infectious Disease and Immu.Immunology: Innate and adaptive immune responses; antigen presentation; immune cell signaling; immune memory; autoimmune disease studies; immunotherapy.
Microbiology Infectious Disease and Immu.Microbiome andCommunity Ecology: Experiments on microbial communities in hosts or environments; effects of diet/antibiotics; functional roles of microbiome; metagenomics plus culturing.

Neuroscience and Behavior.Molecular and Cell Neurobiology: Synapse structure & function; ion channels; neurodevelopment; neurodegenerative disease mechanisms; neural signaling molecules.
Neuroscience and Behavior.Systems and Circuit Neurobiology: Recording or imaging neuronal populations; mapping circuits; optogenetics or chemogenetics; behavioral responses tied to neural circuits.
Neuroscience and Behavior.Behavioral Biology: Animal behavior experiments; learning, cognition, sensory processing; social behavior; mate choice; behavioral ecology.
Neuroscience and Behavior.Cognitive Neuroscience: In animals or humans; experiments probing perception, memory, decision‐making; imaging (fMRI, EEG, MEG) plus behavioral tasks.
Neuroscience and Behavior.Neurophysiology andElectrophysiology: Patch-clamp; in vivo recordings; field potentials; neural dynamics; circuit oscillations; plasticity experiments.

Evolution Ecology and Environmental Biol.Evolutionary Biology: Experimental evolution (microbes, viruses, model organisms) ; adaptation studies; speciation experiments; phylogenetic field work; evolutionary developmental biology (eco-evo-devo).
Evolution Ecology and Environmental Biol.Ecology: Field experiments; community ecology; species interactions; population dynamics; ecosystem function; trophic experiments; climate change impacts.
Evolution Ecology and Environmental Biol.Conservation Biology: Monitoring biodiversity; habitat restoration trials; genetic rescue; experimental interventions in conservation; impact of human activities.
Evolution Ecology and Environmental Biol.Physiological and Environmental Ecology: Organismal responses to temperature, humidity, pollution; stress and acclimation; ecophysiology; plant / animal physiology in natural settings.
Evolution Ecology and Environmental Biol.Microbial Ecology andBiogeochemistry: Carbon/nitrogen cycling; soil microbes; microbial mediation of elemental cycles; experiments on microbial function in ecosystems.

Plant Science.Plant Physiology: Photosynthesis, respiration; water relations; nutrient uptake; stress responses to drought, pests, etc.
Plant Science.Plant Growth and Development: Meristem function; flowering control; seed germination; root architecture; tissue differentiation; plant regeneration.
Plant Science.Plant Pathology and Pests: Plant diseases; fungal, bacterial, viral pathogens; pest resistance; crop protection experiments.
Plant Science.Plant Genetics and Breeding: Creation of new crop varieties; quantitative trait studies; gene mapping; molecular breeding; genetic engineering of plants.
Plant Science.Plant Ecology Agronomy: Plant interactions with environment; crop yields under different agronomic practices; field trials; plant community ecology.

Biomedical and Translational Biology.Cancer Biology: Experiments on oncogenes/tumor suppressors; cell lines and in vivo cancer models; metastasis; drug resistance; therapeutics discovery.
Biomedical and Translational Biology.Development of Therapeutics and Drugs: Drug discovery pipelines; high‐throughput screening; pharmacodynamics/pharmacokinetics; validation in cells and animal models; clinical translational research.
Biomedical and Translational Biology.Regenerative Medicine and Tissue Enginee: Scaffold design; cell therapies; organoids; transplantation; biomaterials; stem cell based repair.
Biomedical and Translational Biology.Neurobiology of Disease: Mechanisms of neurological disorders; animal disease models; neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation; testing interventions.
Biomedical and Translational Biology.Infectious Disease Therapy andVaccine De: Vaccine trials; antiviral/antibiotic therapies; immune adjuvant development; diagnostics development.

Systems Biology Biotechnology and Synthe.Systems Biology: Integration of multiple data types; perturbation experiments; regulatory network mapping; feedback loops; modeling plus experimental validation.
Systems Biology Biotechnology and Synthe.Synthetic Biology: Design and building of new biological circuits; genetic engineering of organisms; cell or pathway redesign; minimal cells; engineering microbes for new functions.
Systems Biology Biotechnology and Synthe.Biotechnology and Bioengineering: Applied experiments: bioproducts; bioreactors; industrial enzymes; metabolic engineering; scale‐up; biomanufacturing.
Systems Biology Biotechnology and Synthe.Omics‐Technologies and High‐Throughput M: Development and use of next‐gen sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, single‐cell and spatial omics; screening technologies.
Systems Biology Biotechnology and Synthe.Bioinformatics with Experimental Validat: Computational predictions verified via wet‐lab experiments; experimental benchmarking of pipelines; cross-validation of high-throughput data.
